Candidates that turned out to be duplicates of prior findings were discarded: portfolio-performance dead PropertyCard onClick (dup of code-review-ppt-web-ui-portfolio-dashboard-deadnav 2026-09-05), BookFacilityPage silent availability error (dup of code-review-ppt-web-ui-facilities-booking-silent-errors), ContentModerationPage window.location full-reload (dup of code-review-ppt-web-ui-content-mod-window-location-nav 2026-08-11). The two findings below are the genuinely-new, non-duplicate issues located in unmined features (rentals, critical-notifications).

evidence: The wired rentals feature has NO error-state path for failed data loads. frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/rentals.tsx contains 6 read useQuery() calls (lines 266, 274, 328, 401, 449, 546) and 0 references to isError (`grep -c isError` on the file returns 0). Every read query destructures only `{ data, isLoading }`.

On query failure (network drop / 4xx / 5xx) each route falls the data back to an empty collection: rentals.tsx:283-284 `const bookings = (data?.data?.data ?? []).map(...)` / `const connections = (connData?.data ?? []).map(...)`; also :375, :418, :558. So a failed load renders as legitimately-empty data, not an error.

RentalsDashboardPageRoute (rentals.tsx:262-320) is the worst case: on a failed reservations query it computes statistics from `bookings = []` and shows totalBookings 0, totalRevenue €0, 0 active/upcoming (rentals.tsx:290-299) with isLoading already false and no error banner — a misleading zeroed revenue dashboard that looks like real empty state to a property manager.

The presentational pages cannot surface the error even if the container knew about it: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/rentals/pages/RentalsDashboardPage.tsx props (lines 10-27) expose `isLoading?: boolean` and `isTaxSummaryLoading?` but NO error/isError prop; same for BookingsPage/CalendarPage/PlatformConnectionsPage/GuestRegistrationPage/BookingDetailPage (none reference isError/.error/catch). The UI layer offers no error affordance at all.

This is a DISTINCT issue from the prior rentals findings, which were all about MUTATIONS and are already done: code-review-ppt-web-core-rentals-mutation-silent, code-review-ppt-web-core-rentals-auth-nonnull-mutation, code-review-ppt-web-core-mutation-no-onerror. Those drove the elaborate mutation onError handling now in the file (handleRentalsMutationError at rentals.tsx:244-260, SESSION_LOST_CODES, AuthError routing) — which makes the untouched READ queries the glaring remaining gap. No prior *ppt-web-ui*.json or backlog row covers the read-query/no-error-prop path (verified against 172 prior ppt-web-ui signals + backlog).

Landable remedy (frontend-only, no backend/KMP): destructure `isError`/`error` from the 6 read useQuery calls, add an `isError?: boolean` (or `loadError`) prop to the rentals presentational pages, and render an error state (retry affordance) instead of defaulting to `?? []`. Matches how the rest of ppt-web surfaces query failures (e.g. PortfolioDashboardPage.tsx:258 `cardsQuery.isError ? <error> : ...`). Severity medium: silent empty/zeroed revenue dashboard on a live, router-mounted feature. Confidence medium: statically code-verified (isError literally never referenced in the container; pages have no error prop), not runtime-confirmed.

The critical-notifications feature renders user-facing emergency copy as hardcoded English with no useTranslation / i18n keys. frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/critical-notifications/components/CriticalNotificationModal.tsx: 'Critical Notification' (:74), 'Posted on {date}' (:88), '{n} of {n}' (:78), 'Acknowledging...' (:127), 'I Acknowledge - Next' (:130), 'I Acknowledge' (:132). CriticalNotificationBanner.tsx: 'View Now' (:54) and the full banner sentence (:42-45).

Worse than a plain i18n gap: CriticalNotificationBanner.tsx:38-45 does manual English-only pluralization — `{count === 1 ? 'notification' : 'notifications'}` and `{count === 1 ? 'requires' : 'require'}`. This cannot be localized by swapping strings; Slovak/Czech have 3+ plural forms and German differs, so the hardcoded binary English branch is structurally wrong for sk/cs/de (the repo's supported locales).

This is critical/emergency content behind an acknowledgement action — a non-English resident literally cannot read what they are acknowledging (the Modal's acknowledge button and the persistent banner CTA are both unlocalized). i18n gaps in error/acknowledgement copy are the highest-impact ones.

critical-notifications is in UNWIRED_FEATURES (frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/unwired-features.ts:44) — built-but-not-yet-routed, code intentionally retained to wire later. The gap is latent today but will ship the moment the feature is wired; prior runs emit findings for unwired features too (e.g. code-review-ppt-web-ui-portfolio-perf-no-i18n for portfolio-performance, also unwired). Non-duplicate: no prior *ppt-web-ui*.json or backlog row references critical-notifications i18n (the only prior hit, dx-stale-todo-security-comments-faults-critical-notifications, is about stale TODO security comments, unrelated).

Reproduce: `grep -rL useTranslation frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/critical-notifications --include='*.tsx' | grep -v .test.` lists NotificationStatsCard.tsx, CriticalNotificationBanner.tsx and CriticalNotificationModal.tsx as having no i18n wiring.

Landable remedy (frontend-only): introduce `t('criticalNotifications.*')` keys for the literals, use interpolation/ICU plurals (e.g. react-i18next `t('...', { count })`) for the banner count sentence instead of manual English branching, and register keys in the sk/cs/de/en bundles. Low severity (unwired today, mechanical fix), confidence medium (static: literals + missing useTranslation code-verified, not runtime-confirmed).
